# Pinned full uBlock Origin components

Source: user-provided uBlock Origin snapshot, version metadata **1.75.1.10** (exact commit unavailable), upstream <https://github.com/gorhill/uBlock>. Original notices remain in source files; GPL-3.0-or-later license is in `LICENSE.txt`. CSS Tree's MIT license is in `src/lib/csstree/LICENSE`.

`src/` retains the unmodified parser, scriptlet library and full procedural task engine required to regenerate shipped assets. Run `node scripts/build-ublock-assets.mjs` at the repository root after an intentional source update. Generated assets are committed; Xcode does not need Node.js.

`compile.js`, `UBlockRuntime.js` and `UBlockCosmetics.js` are tvOSofaBrowse adapters. The host replaces extension registration/messaging with native preferences, JavaScriptCore compilation and document-start WKUserScript. Pinned scriptlet code is selected by parsed arguments; downloaded lists cannot supply executable JavaScript. Trusted scriptlets are enabled only for the pinned official uAssets copy; custom and remotely updated sources are untrusted.

`UBlockFilters.txt` is a flattened official uAssets snapshot retrieved on 2026-10-11, with individual input digests in `uassets-pin.json` and GPL-3.0 license in `UAssets-LICENSE`. It includes all ten files referenced by `filters.txt`. It is bundled for immediate offline use; updates require a new pinned snapshot and app delivery. Existing AdGuard lists retain their weekly updates.

The current adaptation scope is finalized in **2.21.0**. This is a practical WKWebView integration, not complete uBO WebExtension equivalence.

| Capability | Finalized coverage | Deferred boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Static/dynamic matching | Full pinned engines for navigation, page fetch/async XHR and supported Blob workers; strict-document explanations include the winning rule | Other resources use native content rules; destination/type/URL controls and broader cross-backend reconciliation |
| Scriptlets and cosmetics | 174 library/helper entries, pinned aliases/dependencies/trust gating, full procedural task/action library, entity/regex/path/ancestor scopes and exceptions | Complete AdGuard argument compatibility, network cosmetic modifiers and broader live lifecycle audits |
| Lists and policy | Pinned uAssets, retained downloaded/saved lists, site exceptions and third-party Block/Allow/Use Filters/Inherit | Manual filter entry was intentionally removed; policy interaction verification remains partial |
| Workers | Classic/module/nested same-realm Blob request adapters | HTTP(S), Shared/service workers and foreign Blob realms retain native WebKit fallback; custom-protocol cookie/cancellation gaps are not shipped |
| Substitutions | List-selected page API scriptlets and GET/HEAD fetch query pruning | General redirects/surrogates, broader modifiers and network response-header/body delivery |
| Diagnostics | Bounded scriptlet/DOM source-line events, rejection reasons, native action counters and winning navigation rule | Original network list/line attribution, complete traffic visibility and live blocked-dialog focus verification |
| Preparation | Ready-engine and extended-script snapshots, hostname candidate buckets, compiled/source recovery and isolated background replacement retaining the installed engine | Observed timings describe Simulator/macOS fixtures, not physical-TV performance |

Changing cosmetic policy reloads the document because removal of nodes/attributes/classes is irreversible within that document. Individual DOM queries and regular expressions cannot be preempted; procedural scans defer above 15,000 elements. Deferred work is intentionally outside the finalized 2.21.0 scope.

MAIN scriptlets run in the page world; ISOLATED scriptlets and cosmetics use a named WKContentWorld when available. The isolated runtime is skipped with an explicit native status when the selector is absent. Observers stop on page destruction and pause/resume across page-cache navigation. Work is batched between selectors; individual DOM queries cannot be interrupted. Documents above 15,000 elements defer procedural scans until a later mutation, with diagnostic accounting.


Network core (2.21.0): retain the complete upstream static network matcher, hostname firewall and URL filtering engines, with their 20-module dependency closure in UBlockNetwork.js. network.js is the host adapter. JavaScriptCore owns this bundle on a dedicated serial worker, compiles enabled text lists including DNS/HOSTS sources, and caches ready optimized snapshots with engine/PSL fingerprint validation and compiled/source recovery across launches and master-toggle changes. Candidate engines build on isolated queues while the installed engine continues matching; only the newest successful candidate is published. Request matching preserves dynamic URL → hostname firewall → static precedence, including noop fallback. Native navigation actions use asynchronous bounded decisions for explicit main_frame and sub_frame filters; site exceptions bypass the core.

This delivers the matching core, not a complete WebExtension host. Existing WebKit content rules still enforce other resource paths. The page-world UBlockRequests.js adapter gates fetch and asynchronous XMLHttpRequest through a capability-checked WKScriptMessageHandlerWithReply bridge. Only URL, method and API kind cross into the native host; origin comes from the native frame information. Allowed requests retain native WebKit networking. Replies are bounded (250 ms native / 300 ms page fail-open), and obsolete document/policy replies cancel waiting requests. The adapter precedes upstream scriptlets so their request wrappers can compose with it.

XHR keeps its native constructor and allowed-response path, snapshots mutable bodies at send, cancels pending decisions on abort/open/pagehide, and counts timeout from send including the decision delay. A blocked XHR uses status 0, DONE, error and loadend without a successful synthetic response. Gate failures dispatch synthetic events (isTrusted=false); loadstart for allowed requests occurs when native send begins after the decision. Synchronous XHR bypasses the bridge; it must not spin or block the page thread. Incompatible prototype descriptors leave XHR native and are reported as unavailable.

The deferred boundaries are listed in the finalized capability matrix above; strict-document matching, supported Blob-worker adapters and site third-party policy are delivered. The native host's URL shim supports parser hostname normalization only; it does not enable URL-transform modifiers. Coverage reports this boundary. The PublicSuffixList.dat snapshot comes from the retained Firefox iOS reference at revision 371a1b51c54645dbcbd7ad41d1479c7a9e5850f8 (Shared/effective_tld_names.dat), retains its MPL 2.0 notice and is not represented as the latest PSL. network-pin.json records provenance and digests.

`domains.js` is the extended-domain applicability adapter. `UBlockDomains.js` includes the upstream PSL implementation and a generated pinned suffix trie so documents do not parse the textual PSL. Regex/path matching follows StaticExtFilteringHostnameDB; ancestors come from WebKit location.ancestorOrigins, without reading cross-origin parent DOM. Ancestor matching applies to scriptlets, as in upstream. No public-suffix guess from the last two labels is used. RegExp evaluation, like a DOM query, cannot be preempted.

Debug native resource observations use the capability-checked private WebKit content-rule action callback. A bounded buffer stores only action flags, without request URLs. Live Simulator callback delivery is confirmed; allowed traffic, resource type/worker context and exact original rule attribution are not provided by that callback. This is observation, not a blocking delegate or new HTTP-worker full-core adapter.

Query pruning uses the upstream filterQuery/removeparam implementation for nonblocked GET/HEAD decisions. The native and page adapters both constrain the returned URL to the same origin/path/fragment; fetch keeps native Request options. Supported Blob workers inherit this fetch path. POST, asynchronous XHR, navigation and other native resources do not apply these core modifier results yet. No synthetic response or response-header/body substitution is introduced.

The library also includes 21 pinned text-injectable JavaScript resources from upstream redirect-resources.js, with original licenses, aliases and trust flags. These are `+js` surrogates, not a delivered general network redirect backend. All 174 library/helper entries parse; the bundled uAssets snapshot has zero unknown-scriptlet-name rejections after this extension.

Site third-party policy (2.21.0) sends Block/Allow/Noop host rules to the full core and selects corresponding cached native variants. Native variants append actions to each chunk; Noop retains static filtering. Converted source chunks are cached by filter identity. Destination/type/URL policy controls and reconciliation remain pending beyond this UI surface.

Advanced rejection accounting (2.21.0) parses HTML filter syntax with the pinned parser capability enabled but does not emit response-body rules. Valid HTML and header filters report pending delivery separately from malformed syntax. The pinned list has 130 HTML-response, six response-header and one syntax rejection; counts describe this snapshot, not downloaded lists.

Strict-document matching (2.21.0) bundles the pinned traffic.js decision and hostname-validation helpers in strict.js with original GPL notice. Explicit document filters and validated generic hostname filters retain upstream important/exception precedence. The host shows a native blocked-navigation explanation including the winning filter from traffic.js strict-decision logData or the upstream dynamic engine toLogData. Reading only the last static probe would misattribute explicit/generic precedence. The rule stays in native memory/UI, is not written to logs or returned to page scripts, and does not claim original list/line provenance. No temporary allow-once mechanism is claimed. Destination site exceptions apply before main navigation matching, and policy-generation changes cancel obsolete decisions.

## Preparation, document lifecycle and cache maintenance

`BrowserAdBlockService` owns source preferences, downloads, policy variants, compilation caches, full-core preparation and native rule installation. Native conversion/WebKit compilation, full-network preparation and extended-script preparation start independently; a single joined completion preserves the existing deferred reload policy. Native preprocessing uses its own locked JS context, while each extended compilation owns a separate context. Debug app Swift and the separate native-converter package are optimized for filter preparation; Debug instrumentation remains compiled in. The WebView keeps document generations, installed scripts and native UI/lifecycle decisions. Native rules apply as soon as available; extended preparation emits one final completion. Failed updates preserve installed rules, and partial results are not cached as complete policies. Successful partial protection is still usable on a cold start.

Background reloads defer while fullscreen/media/input/dialog state is busy or an iframe is opaque. Exiting fullscreen requests another safe check; a still-playing inline video, edited field or opaque iframe keeps the upgrade registered for the next navigation/manual reload. Explicit preference changes still request their deliberate reload. The live document's bridge token remains valid until document replacement; page-cache markers restore the cached document token. Input dirtiness is tracked from document start in every frame, independently of filter readiness.

Extended rules use lazy hostname/entity candidate buckets. Generic, regex and ancestor scopes remain in a conservative fallback; path constraints and exclusions still use the original applicability matcher. Original source order is retained. Documents materialize only candidate rule records; WebKit still receives shared script source, so this is not a claim that injected source bytes or measured frame load time decreased. This adapts uBO's hostname database retrieval without its synchronous WebExtension messaging host.

Extended compilation pulls parser records in batches of at most 512 under scoped autorelease pools. Each record crosses as complete JSON plus routing metadata, avoiding a second nested rule-object graph in Swift. Escape bucket payloads directly into the final script buffer, release consumed buffers, scope hostname-normalization temporaries and discard the compilation parser context before script assembly. All selected records, source order, exceptions and scriptlet dependencies are retained. This adapts the serialized-record mechanism of upstream `static-filtering-io.js`; the tvOS host pulls batches instead of retaining extension writer blocks. The parser's collecting API remains available to existing tooling, and its upstream `finish()` releases the last CSS parser string.

In a standalone macOS Debug-source profile with the bundled uAssets and six downloaded AdGuard lists, final peak process RSS decreased from 759 MiB to 385 MiB (the original whole-result implementation peaked at 1,770 MiB). All 13,871 MAIN and 135,990 ISOLATED ordered records, bucket membership, runtime code, indexes, fallback selection, declarations/function maps and per-source counters/rejections matched the original output. JSON key order and escaping change the source bytes while preserving decoded records. These are compiler-process measurements, not a physical-TV app memory budget or confirmation that every jetsam cause is resolved.

A user-requested Rebuild Filters advances a persistent generation salt in the filter identity. All three backends rebuild from existing enabled source text; normal launches reuse the new generation's caches. It does not delete website data, change enabled sources or fetch updates. Record the preparation completion date and monotonic wall duration only after a successful rebuilt pipeline; cache-only restores do not replace that record. Separately record the total time until a visible main document confirms its matching prepared policy through its pageshow marker. Explicit Rebuild Filters requests one page reload after readiness, rather than deferring indefinitely on opaque iframes; ordinary background updates retain their busy-document safeguards.

Prepared MAIN/ISOLATED scripts persist under `BrowserExtendedRules` with source identity, bundled asset fingerprint and an explicit adapter schema. The current schema is `extended-v3`; bump it when changing the native script generator. Invalid cache shapes rebuild from source. Failed replacement compilation retains the installed runtime. Network/extended snapshots retain the successful current cache and one previous cache after successful restore/write, including a previous extended schema. Native store cleanup uses WebKit enumeration/removal APIs, preserving all installed identifiers, three policy manifests and in-flight compilation. It only removes superseded generated rule caches; downloaded lists, preferences and website data remain separate.

## Reproducible uAssets refresh

Choose an immutable 40-character commit from the official uAssets repository and record the retrieval date explicitly:

```sh
node scripts/update-uassets-snapshot.mjs --revision <commit-sha> --date YYYY-MM-DD --checkout <local-uAssets-checkout>
# Or retrieve exactly that commit from the official raw GitHub host:
node scripts/update-uassets-snapshot.mjs --revision <commit-sha> --date YYYY-MM-DD --download
```

The local mode reads committed files with `git show`, ignoring working-tree edits, and requires the official origin. The tool recursively flattens relative filter includes at their original position, preserves conditional directives and upstream notices, rejects cycles/unsupported paths, and retrieves the upstream license. It completes all input reads and validation before staging output replacements. The pin records the commit, entry file, each input SHA-256, flattened output SHA-256, license SHA-256 and retrieval date. Reusing the same commit/date produces the same snapshot metadata. Review the three resulting files together, then build/deliver the app; updating filter text alone does not require regenerating the pinned engine/scriptlet code.

The existing 2026-10-11 snapshot is unchanged and has no known exact commit; its original input digests are retained rather than inventing provenance. Future refreshes use the new commit-based workflow. The settings date comes from bundled `uassets-pin.json`. The updater is a maintenance tool, not an automatic network updater, and does not execute downloaded filter text.
